He is a pretty shy and quiet guy, so he didn’t tell many people about it before he left and I doubt he was going to when he got back if I didn’t do this. I thought that he needed recognition for the great work he was doing, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him to tell all of his friends and family who he hadn’t told about this trip. I did this while he was away, about a week before he got home. Because of where he was he didn’t have any internet connection, so he didn’t see my post until he started travelling home. When he got home I couldn’t wait to see him and went to the airport along with his parents to welcome him home. He seemed kind of annoyed at me at the airport, but said he was fine and was clearly very happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and that he just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask again what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn’t want any sort of attention for what he was doing, he didn’t want everyone thinking he just went there to brag that he’s such a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self improvement, not to help volunteer, he felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all of his friends and family about it. He said he didn’t want the attention of that post, and I shouldn’t of made it without asking him, especially when I knew he wouldn’t see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him, I didn’t say anything bad. AITA for making that post?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by making that Facebook post about my best friend. Let me start by going through the situation again to make sure I understand all the details. My best friend went on a three-month trip to India to do volunteer work. He helped build a water pipeline and taught kids about hygiene and sanitation. That's pretty impressive, right? He also paid for the entire trip himself, which cost over $3000. He's a pretty shy and quiet guy, so I don't think he told many people about it before he left. I was worried he wouldn't tell people when he got back either, especially since he's so shy. I thought he needed recognition for the great work he did, so I decided to make a Facebook post about him. I did this while he was away, about a week before he came home. Because of where he was, he didn't have any internet connection, so he didn't see my post until he started traveling home. When he got home, I went to the airport with his parents to welcome him. He seemed a bit annoyed with me at the airport but said he was fine and was clearly happy to see his parents. I thought we would hang out together the day we got home, but he said no and just wanted to go home and rest. I decided to text him that evening to ask what was wrong. He told me he was pissed off at me for the Facebook post. He said he didn't want any attention for what he was doing, didn't want everyone thinking he went there just to brag about being a great person, and that the only reason he really went was for self-improvement, not to help volunteer. He felt selfish enough about his reasons for going without my post telling all his friends and family about it. He said he didn't want the attention of that post and that I shouldn't have made it without asking him, especially since I knew he wouldn't see it for another week. I was kind of annoyed at him because I thought I was doing a really nice thing, since he would be too shy to tell people about it himself. The post was so positive about him; I didn't say anything bad. So, the question is: Did I do the right thing by making that post? Is it AITA (Ask If It's Too Awkward) for making that post? Let me break this down. First, I need to consider my friend's feelings and his reasons for being upset. He's shy and didn't want attention for his volunteer work. He went for self-improvement, not to help others, and he felt that my post made it seem like he was bragging or seeking attention. He also mentioned that I shouldn't have made the post without asking him, especially since he wouldn't see it for another week. On my side, I thought I was doing something nice by recognizing his efforts, especially since he's shy and wouldn't tell others himself. I didn't mean any harm, and the post was positive. Now, I need to evaluate whether my actions were appropriate or if they crossed a line. Here are some points to consider: 1. **Respect for Privacy**: My friend didn't tell many people about his trip, and he's shy. By posting about him without his consent, I might have invaded his privacy. He might have had reasons for not sharing it publicly, and I didn't consider that. 2. **Intent vs. Impact**: My intention was to recognize his efforts and share something positive. However, the impact was that it made him uncomfortable and upset. It's possible that my good intentions didn't align with his feelings about the situation. 3. **Communication**: I didn't ask him before posting. If I had communicated with him, maybe he would have expressed his feelings about it, and I could have avoided the situation. 4. **His Reasons for Going**: He mentioned that he went for self-improvement, not to help others. My post might have misrepresented his intentions, making it seem like he was more focused on helping others than he actually was. 5. **Feeling of Being Judged**: He felt that the post made it seem like he was bragging or seeking attention, which he didn't want. This could have made him feel judged or misunderstood. 6. **Timing**: I knew he wouldn't see the post for another week, so I didn't give him a chance to respond or express his feelings before posting. This could have contributed to his frustration. Considering all these points, it seems like I might have overstepped by posting about him without his consent. While my intentions were good, they didn't take into account his feelings and privacy. It's important to respect his wishes and understand that he might have had valid reasons for not wanting to share his trip publicly. In the future, it would be better to communicate with him before sharing personal or sensitive information about him. This way, I can ensure that I'm respecting his boundaries and that my actions align with his feelings. So, in conclusion, while I thought I was doing something nice, it might have been AITA because it didn't consider his feelings and privacy. It's important to respect his wishes and communicate before sharing such information.
